// purpose: @debuggen/telemetry - the compiler project for the monorepo typecheck gate. `pnpm typecheck` (= `pnpm demo:generate && tsc -b`) builds the root solution file, whose `references` list this project directly after packages/shared: telemetry sits one level above the bottom of the acyclic package graph (AAP 0.2.2) and depends on that one workspace and nothing else. So `references` below has exactly one entry, and `tsc -b` on either the root solution or this project alone builds packages/shared's declarations first.
// format: Strict JSON, like tsconfig.base.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` can read it, so no consumer has to know which one to reach for. tsc, ESLint, Vitest, tsup and Prettier all accept comments in a tsconfig, but the rationale for each decision is recorded in the `"// …"` string keys of this object instead. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// two-runtimes: This is the only project in the monorepo that legitimately spans two runtimes in one program (see the `lib` note): the runtime-neutral library (schema, redaction, correlation, aggregates), the page-injected browser agent under src/browser/** and the dev-server Node preload under src/node/**. Splitting it is deliberately NOT done - the AAP names a single tsconfig.json for this workspace and the root solution references only this file - so the discipline that keeps the two runtimes apart lives elsewhere: eslint.config.js (`no-restricted-imports`) forbids `@debuggen/protocol` and `@debuggen/shared/node` inside src/browser/**, and esbuild.agent.mjs hard-fails if the agent bundle pulls in a Node builtin. The compiler's job here is to type-check all three subtrees in one pass; the conventions recorded in the `"// cross-runtime-conventions"` key below are what keep that honest.
// inherited: Everything not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, the no-unused/no-implicit diagnostics, `target` ES2023 and the declaration-emit settings (`declaration`, `declarationMap`, `sourceMap`, `emitDeclarationOnly`, `incremental`). `noEmit` must never be added: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects a referenced project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because the root solution file references this project and a non-composite reference fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate at this project.
// compilerOptions.module: The base defaults to "ESNext" + "bundler" for the bundled/web workspaces and instructs Node-targeted projects - naming the `./node/register` preload entry of this package - to override with NodeNext. package.json declares `"type": "module"`, and dist/node/register.mjs is loaded directly by Node (`NODE_OPTIONS=--import`) inside the developer's `next dev` process, so this project is type-checked under real Node ESM resolution rather than a bundler approximation. Mirrors packages/shared and AAP 0.3.4 ("NodeNext for node packages"). Consequence for every source file in src/**: relative specifiers must carry an explicit ".js" extension - `./schema/event.js`, `./browser/fiber-diff.js`, and `./react.js` for a module authored as react.tsx - and directory specifiers must name the file (`"./node/index.js"`). Extensionless relative imports are a compile error here by design (TS2835); they would break the real Node consumer of the preload. tsup/esbuild resolve a "./x.js" specifier from a TypeScript importer back to "./x.ts" (or ".tsx"), so the library bundle, the agent IIFE and the preload are unaffected. `verbatimModuleSyntax` is inherited, so a specifier imported only for its types must be written `import type` / `export type`: the agent IIFE and the preload must not retain a runtime import that existed only for a type.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: Per-workspace (the base deliberately leaves it unset), so the declaration tree under .tsbuild/ mirrors src/ exactly: src/index.ts -> .tsbuild/index.d.ts and src/node/register.ts -> .tsbuild/node/register.d.ts, matching the paths the package.json `exports` map advertises under dist/. It also pins the program's boundary: nothing outside src/ may be an input (see the fixture notes under `"// include"`, `"// exclude"` and `"// exclude.fixtures"`).
// compilerOptions.lib: Widened from the base's ES2023-only set, which exists so that a Node-only package cannot reference `window` and still compile. This project must type the browser agent, which legitimately uses `window`, `document`, `PerformanceObserver`, `PerformanceEventTiming`, `PerformanceResourceTiming`, `fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest`, `MutationObserver` and `window.postMessage`, while the same program also types the Node preload. DOM.Iterable is what makes `for (const e of performanceObserverEntryList)`-style iteration and `Headers`/`FormData` iteration type-check. ES2023 is restated alongside the browser libs because `lib` REPLACES the inherited array rather than merging with it - omitting ES2023 here would silently drop `Array.prototype.findLast`, `toSorted` and the rest. The cost of one program over two runtimes is paid in the source: see the cross-runtime conventions below. In particular the runtime-neutral modules (src/schema/**, src/redaction/**, src/correlation/**, src/aggregate/**) must not assume a DOM just because the compiler now knows one exists.
// compilerOptions.types: The base sets no `types` so that one workspace's ambient globals cannot bleed into another. This package needs exactly one: @types/node 24.13.6 (a root devDependency, resolved through the workspace-root node_modules/@types). It types the `node:*` builtins and the OpenTelemetry/Prisma surfaces used by src/node/**, and it is authored to stand down from the DOM globals it shares with lib.dom.d.ts, so the two coexist in this program. @types/react is a devDependency of this package but is deliberately absent here: it is not an ambient global package. The JSX types of the one .tsx source (src/browser/react.test.tsx, AAP 0.8.3) arrive through the automatic runtime's `react/jsx-runtime` module import, and `import type { ... } from "react"` resolves the same way. Listing it in `types` would instead make React's globals ambient across the browser agent and the preload.
// compilerOptions.jsx: Inherited from the base (React 19.3.0 automatic runtime) and restated so the guarantee is local: the colocated `*.test.tsx` under src/browser/** is inside `include`, so this project must be able to compile JSX without an `import React` in every file. A base that later scoped jsx to the React surfaces would otherwise break this project's tests.
// compilerOptions.not-set: NOT overridden: "outDir" / "declarationDir" / "tsBuildInfoFile". The base anchors them per project with `${configDir}`, which resolves to the directory of THIS file, so declarations and the incremental stamp land in packages/telemetry/.tsbuild - ignored by .gitignore, .prettierignore and the ignore list in eslint.config.js. A repository-level path such as ../../.tsbuild/packages/telemetry would be a new output location outside those ignore lists and would leak build artefacts into `git status`; tsc must likewise never write into packages/telemetry/dist, which belongs to tsup, esbuild.agent.mjs and esbuild.node.mjs and holds the artefacts the `exports` map points at. NOT set: "paths" / "baseUrl". `@debuggen/shared` resolves through the pnpm workspace symlink and that package's `exports` map plus the project reference below, exactly as the runtime and the bundlers resolve it (AAP 0.2.2); aliasing to source would hide a broken `exports` map and let the acyclic package layering be violated without anything failing. NOT set: "resolveJsonModule" (the base already enables it) - but see the fixture note below: JSON under test/ is loaded at runtime, never imported. NOT set: "noEmit", and no strictness flag is relaxed on top of the base.
// include: src/** only - both extensions, because Vitest collects this package's suites from `packages/telemetry/src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` and the React fiber-hook test is authored as .tsx. The colocated `*.test.ts(x)` files are deliberately part of the program so the typecheck gate covers them: `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` apply to tests exactly as they do to sources. Tests import `{ describe, it, expect }` from "vitest" explicitly rather than relying on globals, so no "vitest/globals" entry is needed in `types`.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list; resolved relative to this directory, so it means packages/telemetry/dist, packages/telemetry/node_modules and packages/telemetry/test/fixtures. `include` already restricts the input set to src/**, which leaves dist/ (bundler output), .tsbuild/ (declaration output) and test/ outside the program; the entries here document that intent and keep it true if `include` is ever widened. Note what `exclude` does NOT do: it filters the `include` globs only, so a file reached by an import still joins the program. The rules recorded under `"// exclude.fixtures"`, not this list, are what keep test/ out.
// exclude.fixtures: The fixture pitfall, with the exact compiler behaviour of this project. Importing TypeScript from outside src/ - `import { x } from "../test/helpers/x.js"` - fails hard, with TS6059 ("is not under 'rootDir'") plus TS6307 ("is not listed within the file list of project"). Keeping test/ free of TypeScript is what lets `rootDir` stay "src". Importing JSON - `import fixture from "../test/fixtures/event.json" with { type: "json" }` - is not rejected, because `emitDeclarationOnly` means that file emits nothing and so never trips the rootDir check. That is the trap: it compiles, silently adds an input that sits outside `include`, the declaration mirror and the Vitest/lint boundary, and gives the test an unvalidated `any`-shaped literal typed by the fixture rather than by the schema. Fixture-driven tests therefore read the file at runtime - JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../../test/fixtures/<name>.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")) - and validate the parsed value with the Zod schema from src/schema/event.ts, which is the assertion that matters anyway.
// references: The ONLY project reference. @debuggen/telemetry depends on @debuggen/shared and on no other workspace (AAP 0.2.2 edge list), and `tsc -b` therefore builds packages/shared's declarations before this project. Never add ../protocol, ../code-analysis, ../panel-schema, ../instrumentation or any app: protocol and the rest sit ABOVE telemetry, importing them is an eslint `no-restricted-imports` failure, and a reference here would create precisely the cycle the layering exists to prevent. `SourceLocation` - the one symbol this package consumes from shared - comes from that package's root entry ("."), which is browser-safe. src/browser/** may import that entry but must never touch `@debuggen/shared/node` (hashing, safe-fs) or a Node builtin: it is bundled into an IIFE injected into the developer's page at `document_start`.
// cross-runtime-conventions: Cross-runtime source conventions this configuration forces on src/**. Because lib.dom.d.ts and @types/node are both in scope, the compiler will accept code that cannot run in one of the two runtimes. These are the failure modes that surface first, and the rules that avoid them. 1. Timer handles are `ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>`, never `number` and never `NodeJS.Timeout`: the DOM and Node overloads disagree on the return type, and either concrete spelling breaks in the other runtime. 2. `startTime` is Unix epoch MILLISECONDS as a double, in both subtrees - the browser computes `performance.timeOrigin + entry.startTime`, the preload converts an OpenTelemetry `hrTime` tuple - and `duration` is milliseconds. That single time base is what lets the correlator order browser, server and db events in one trace. 3. Environment-specific globals are reached behind capability checks - `typeof PerformanceObserver !== "undefined"`, `typeof window !== "undefined"` - not behind casts, so the runtime-neutral modules never assume a DOM and stay importable by the service and the preload. 4. Shared helpers prefer `globalThis` over `window`/`global`. The span helper is installed at `globalThis.__DEBUGGEN__` in BOTH runtimes and must keep the identical shape { span<T>(name: string, meta: Record<string, unknown>, fn: () => T): T } that packages/instrumentation/src/patch/wrap-template.ts emits and that scripts/check-no-residual-instrumentation.mjs greps for. Changing that shape breaks every patched function in a developer's project.
